gloss: report to the throne; memorial to the emperor

definitions.gloss: report to the throne; memorial to the emperor
definitions.explanation: A formal report or petition submitted to the emperor by a minister or official. A historical and legal term, used mainly of the imperial court and of government under the Meiji Constitution; it does not describe reporting to an ordinary superior.

examples.japanese: {大臣|だいじん}が{天皇|てんのう}に{上奏|じょうそう}した。
examples.english: The minister submitted a report to the emperor.

examples.japanese: その{案|あん}は{上奏|じょうそう}されたが、{採用|さいよう}されなかった。
examples.english: The proposal was submitted to the throne, but it was not adopted.

examples.japanese: {明治|めいじ}{憲法|けんぽう}のもとでは、{内閣|ないかく}が{重要|じゅうよう}な{事項|じこう}を{上奏|じょうそう}する{仕組|しく}みになっていた。
examples.english: Under the Meiji Constitution, the cabinet was structured so as to report important matters to the throne.

notes:
{上|じょう} (upward) + {奏|そう} (to report to a superior). Used as a noun and with する.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {上奏|じょうそう}する: to report to the throne
- {上奏文|じょうそうぶん}: a written memorial to the emperor
- {上奏|じょうそう}{権|けん}: the right to report directly to the emperor

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {奏上|そうじょう}: the same act, with the characters reversed; interchangeable in most contexts
- {報告|ほうこく}: report — the everyday word, used for any superior or audience
